text:
maria - sec: heads-up: Snyk + OSS-Intel just surfaced CVE-2026-4021 affecting xmlsec (integer overflow). Affects our SAML assertion parsing in auth-proxy and the java-saml-bridge. listing: https://ossvuln.example/CVE-2026-4021 :warning:
ashok - infra: thanks — any EPSS/CVSS numbers yet?
maria - sec: initial feed: CVSS 7.8 (High), EPSS 0.62. Exploit maturity: PoC claimed on a public repo but not widespread exploit chatter yet.
sec-bot: automated-scan: found 4 services with xmlsec <= 2.2.9: auth-proxy, java-saml-bridge, telemetry-agent, legacy-sshauth. See /security/scan/reports/212500.
olivia - sre: can we confirm runtime exposure? auth-proxy parses external SAML from identity providers — that's customer-facing. java-saml-bridge talks to IdP only. telemetry-agent consumes SAML from internal tests only.
paul - platform: inventory check: auth-proxy in k8s (prod/us-west1, prod/eu-west1) deployed via helm chart v3.2. telemetry-agent is a daemonset in monitoring cluster.
maria - sec: quick triage suggestions: 1) mark auth-proxy as highest priority (internet-facing) 2) check KMS-wrapped keys for SAML signing — ensure no key exposure 3) enable audit logging for SAML verification failures 4) prepare patch/rollback plan.
ashok - infra: patch path: upstream xmlsec patch available in 2.2.10. For java-saml-bridge (Maven) we'll update dependency and run full test matrix. For auth-proxy (Go wrapper) we vendor a fixed binary or rebuild with patched libxmlsec and run canary.
olivia - sre: proposed rollout: canary in prod/us-west1 with 10% traffic, 30m soak, then ramp. If we need faster mitigation we can add a runtime filter to drop SAML responses with abnormal length/structures (mitigation heuristic).
paul - platform: RBAC question — if we push new images to our registry we need a short-lived deploy token for the canary pipeline. Should we create a one-off service account with limited scope?
maria - sec: yes, create a temporary deploy service account scoped to registry:write and k8s:deploy in prod/us-west1 only. Add an audit log entry in the ticket and rotate creds after rollout.
nashok - infra: creating deploy SA now. Command (internal):
```
# create short-lived k8s service account
kubectl create serviceaccount cve-2026-4021-deployer -n infra-cd
kubectl create token cve-2026-4021-deployer --duration=1h -n infra-cd
```
olivia - sre: can someone validate whether our KMS integration for signing is impacted? If SAML keys are in KMS, a compromise of xml parsing doesn't leak KMS keys but could allow signature verification bypass — need to check.
maria - sec: confirm: KMS stores signing keys (not raw private keys on disk). No KMS compromise reported. Still, we should add an audit filter: log all signature verification failures to secure audit index for 90 days.
sec-bot: logged action: created ticket SEC-2026-4021 with owner maria, severity: HIGH, due: 2125080000.
paul - platform: patch ETA: auth-proxy rebuild + canary in 3 hours, java-saml-bridge PR in 6 hours, telemetry-agent patch in 12 hours.
maria - sec: mitigation checklist (short):
- [ ] create deploy SA + token (ashok)
- [ ] rebuild auth-proxy with patched xmlsec (ashok)
- [ ] open PR for java-saml-bridge (paul)
- [ ] enable SAML verification audit logs (paul)
- [ ] run fuzz test on patched binaries (olivia)
- [ ] update incident page + customer comms draft (maria)

ashok - infra: started rebuild, pushing canary image tag cve-2026-4021-canary to internal-registry.
olivia - sre: canary smoke steps: 1) health checks green 2) auth flow end-to-end with Google IdP 3) synthetic SAML invalid payloads validated rejected 4) monitor SLO error budget for 15m 5) if >1% auth failures rollback.
maria - sec: customer comms draft (short): "We are aware of CVE-2026-4021 impacting XML security libraries used for SAML parsing. We have prioritized the internet-facing auth-proxy and are rolling a patched release. No evidence of active exploitable incidents in our environment; we'll provide updates in SEC-2026-4021." I'll attach to the ticket.
paul - platform: quick note on auditing: make sure CloudAudit logs export to secure-bucket and restrict access to sec-team only. Also add retention 90 days for SAML verification logs.
maria - sec: agreed. olivia, can you run the fuzz harness for SAML inputs against patched binary?
olivia - sre: on it. starting now, will post results here.
sec-bot: fuzz-run started (job id fuzz-212500-1). Estimated 45m.
nashok - infra: canary deployed to prod/us-west1 with tag cve-2026-4021-canary. Watching.
maria - sec: nice. assign owners: auth-proxy -> ashok, java-saml-bridge -> paul, telemetry-agent -> olivia. I'll be primary incident comms.
olivia - sre: fuzz results: no crash-returns in 45m, some malformed inputs rejected properly. Will keep running overnight.
maria - sec: closing loop: severity stays HIGH due to internet-facing parsing + PoC. EPSS 0.62 justifies rapid rollout. If we see exploit attempts we'll escalate to incident channel.
paul - platform: after patch merges, will open backport PR for 1.2.x branch and coordinate with customer-facing release notes.
maria - sec: thanks team. logging action items into SEC-2026-4021 and scheduling postmortem checklist for next week. :white_check_mark:
